why: 2025 preprints report constructive proofs for the previously hardest residue class p ≡ 1 (mod 4) and a semi-constructive approach covering 804 of 840 residue classes mod 840 with the remainder bounded probabilistically, plus improved computational verification to 10^18; these look like genuine incremental case-settling on the conjecture itself, but not full resolution.
queries: Erdős–Straus conjecture Wikipedia article residue classes proven

found.title: Constructive Proofs of the Erdős–Straus Conjecture for Prime Numbers of the Form P≡1(mod4)
found.note: Preprint claiming constructive proof for primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4), historically the hardest residue class; not read.

found.title: Almost a Complete Proof of the Generalized Erdős-Straus Conjecture: 5/a = 1/b + 1/c + 1/d
found.note: Preprint on a generalized (numerator 5) variant of the conjecture, not the classical n≥2 statement; likely does not itself move this bullet.

found.title: Further verification and empirical evidence for the Erdős-Straus conjecture
found.note: Preprint extending computational verification bound to 10^18; existence-search extension, does not by itself move the open question.

found.title: A Divisor Parametrization for the Erdős–Straus Conjecture
found.note: Preprint (2026) offering a semi-constructive approach reportedly covering 804 of 840 residue classes mod 840 with the rest bounded probabilistically; not read.
